change: Recognize physician assistant/associate terminology and jurisdiction-specific collaboration rather than a universal supervision model.
Remove the misleading medical/nonclinical binary; distinguish job title, supervised pre-licensure work and independent clinical licensure.
Add limited delegated nonclinical approvals/benefit-only decisions as a published program alternative; keep medical-necessity denials distinct.
Make retained health-plan appeals explicit in the AZPC delegation example.
Separate NP practice category, furnishing authority and employer conditions; flag prospective/stale availability wording.
Clarify separately authorized pharmacist therapy activity and avoid implying a new physician instruction for every protocol-authorized action.
Add New Mexico additional prescribing-certification example without implying general psychologist prescribing rights.
Use official 2025 codification to distinguish interdisciplinary planning, designated RN coordination, attending, certification and admission; retain edition limit.
Show eligible urgent internal/external review concurrently and qualify applicable plan/process scope.
Add applicable Part 2 protections to prevent treating the HIPAA minimum-necessary treatment exception as unrestricted sharing.
Distinguish documented associate-director direction from manager/supervisor collaboration; do not imply an unsupported direct reporting chain.
Stop using expired/unavailable sources as current proof; replace relevant examples with accessible Noyes/Michigan and care-program sources.
Add specific public context for transport, protection, access-control, billing and legal functions while keeping composite/local mandate limits.
Record tension between a program's professional categories and medical-director final responsibility; do not infer a case signatory without clarification.
Place an explicit product/integrated-plan route check before applying the standard MA path; detailed integrated rules remain outside verified scope.
